title: Evaluating the Activity of R2 Retrotransposons in Mammalian Cells
author: Chen, Luo, et al.
materials: NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix
Countess II FL automated cell counter

This step details the process of transient transfection of reporter vectors into HEK293T cells.7.Plate coating.a.Add 250 μL poly-D-lysine (PDL) at a concentration of 0.1 mg/mL to 24-well plates for 15 min before seeding cells.b.Remove the PDL solution.c.Wash twice with 250 μL 1× phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).Note: Make sure to completely cover each well with 250 μL 1× PBS because of the cytotoxicity of PDL.8.Cell preparation before transfection.a.Culture HEK293T cells using HEK293T cell culture medium in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2. Seed approximately 4 × 106 cells in a 10 cm dish and passage every two days.b.Wash HEK293T cells with 3 mL 1× PBS once.c.Add 3 mL 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA (Gibco) and incubate at 37°C for 3 min.d.Add equal HEK293T cell culture medium (3 mL) and transfer the total cell suspension to 15 mL centrifuge tube.e.Centrifuge the cells at 300 × g for 3 min.f.Remove supernatant, then resuspend cells with 1 mL HEK293T cell culture medium.g.Count total live cells by a cell counter.i.Prepare the sample by mixing 10 μL of cell suspension and 10 μL of 0.4% trypan blue stain.ii.Pipet 10 μL the trypan blue-stained sample into a Countess chamber slide.iii.Count live cells by a cell counter, e.g., Countess II FL automated cell counter.h.Seed approximately 3 × 105 live HEK293T cells in a 24-well PDL coated plate. Make sure cells are about 70% confluence when transfection.5,69.Transfection. For experiments of screening new R2 systems, transfect 250 ng pCAG-R2X-3xFlag plasmid and 250 ng mCherry-pCAG-donor(R2X)-GFP(intron) plasmid to HEK293T cells via Lipofectamine 3000 (Invitrogen) (The R2X means new R2 system, such as R2Tg). The brief steps are as follows.a.Dilute 1.5 μL Lipofectamine 3000 Reagent in 25 μL Opti-MEM Medium. Pipet the mixture up and down gently.b.Prepare mixture of DNA by adding 250 ng pCAG-R2X-3xFlag plasmid and 250 ng mCherry-pCAG-donor(R2X)-GFP(intron) plasmid to 25 μL Opti-MEM Medium, then add 1 μL P3000 Reagent. Pipet the mixture up and down gently.c.Add all of the diluted DNA to the tube of diluted Lipofectamine 3000 Reagent. Pipet the mixture up and down gently and incubate for 15 min at room temperature (about 20°C).d.Pipette dropwise the DNA-lipid complex evenly to cells and shake the wells for even distribution.

steps.title: Replace R2 sequences
steps.instruction: Replace the coding sequence, 5′ UTR and 3′ UTR of the R2 protein with those of the desired R2 element before constructing the plasmids.

steps.title: Coat plates with poly‑D‑lysine
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL of 0.1 mg/mL poly‑D‑lysine to each well of a 24‑well plate, incubate 15 min, discard the solution, then wash twice with 250 µL 1× PBS, making sure the well is completely covered each wash.

steps.title: Prepare and seed HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Culture HEK293T cells at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in appropriate medium; seed ~4 × 10⁶ cells in a 10 cm dish and passage every two days. Wash cells with 3 mL 1× PBS, add 3 mL 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 37 °C 3 min, then add 3 mL fresh medium. Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube, centrifuge 300 × g 3 min, discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL medium. Count live cells by mixing 10 µL cell suspension with 10 µL 0.4 % trypan blue, loading 10 µL into a Countess chamber slide, and using an automated cell counter. Seed ~3 × 10⁵ live cells per PDL‑coated well of the 24‑well plate so that cells are ~70 % confluent at transfection.

substeps.instruction: Culture HEK293T cells at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in appropriate medium.
Seed ~4 × 10⁶ cells in a 10 cm dish; passage every two days.
Wash cells with 3 mL 1× PBS.
Add 3 mL 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 37 °C 3 min.
Add 3 mL fresh medium, transfer to 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge 300 × g 3 min, discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL medium.
Mix 10 µL cells with 10 µL 0.4 % trypan blue, load 10 µL into Countess chamber, count live cells.
Seed ~3 × 10⁵ live cells per PDL‑coated well (≈70 % confluence).

steps.title: Transfect cells with R2 plasmids
steps.instruction: For each well, dilute 1.5 µL Lipofectamine 3000 in 25 µL Opti‑MEM. In a separate tube, combine 250 ng pCAG‑R2X‑3xFlag plasmid and 250 ng mCherry‑pCAG‑donor(R2X)‑GFP(intron) plasmid with 25 µL Opti‑MEM and add 1 µL P3000 reagent; mix gently. Add the DNA mixture to the diluted Lipofectamine, mix gently and incubate 15 min at room temperature (~20 °C). Add the DNA‑lipid complex dropwise to the cells and gently shake the well to distribute evenly.

substeps.instruction: Dilute 1.5 µL Lipofectamine 3000 in 25 µL Opti‑MEM; mix gently.
Add 250 ng each plasmid to 25 µL Opti‑MEM, add 1 µL P3000 reagent; mix gently.
Combine the diluted DNA with the diluted Lipofectamine, mix gently, and incubate 15 min at ~20 °C.
Add the DNA‑lipid complex dropwise to the cells and shake the well for even distribution.

steps.title: Detach cells for flow analysis
steps.instruction: Seven days after transfection, remove supernatant and wash cells with 250 µL 1× PBS. Add 200 µL pre‑warmed 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 37 °C 3 min. Add 200 µL culture medium, transfer all liquid to a 1.5 mL tube and centrifuge 300 × g 3 min. Discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 300 µL 1× PBS and transfer to a 5 mL round‑bottom tube.

substeps.instruction: Remove supernatant and wash cells with 250 µL 1× PBS.
Add 200 µL pre‑warmed 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 37 °C 3 min.
Add 200 µL culture medium, collect all liquid in a 1.5 mL tube, centrifuge 300 × g 3 min.
Remove supernatant, resuspend cells in 300 µL 1× PBS, transfer to a 5 mL round‑bottom tube.

steps.title: Acquire flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Set up the BD LSRFortessa flow cytometer using negative‑control cells (donor‑only transfected) to define parameters. Establish gating: FSC‑A vs SSC‑A to exclude debris, FSC‑H vs FSC‑A to exclude doublets, then SSC‑A vs FITC‑A to gate GFP‑positive cells. Acquire data for approximately 30 000 events per sample.

substeps.instruction: Configure the cytometer with negative‑control cells to set voltage and compensation.
Gate FSC‑A vs SSC‑A to remove debris.
Gate FSC‑H vs FSC‑A to remove doublets.
Gate SSC‑A vs FITC‑A to collect GFP‑positive cells.
Acquire ~30 000 events per sample.

steps.title: Analyze data with FlowJo
steps.instruction: Import the acquired FCS files into FlowJo v.10 and apply the previously defined gates to quantify the percentage of GFP‑positive cells.

description: R2 retrotransposons rely on reverse transcription of RNA intermediates to propagate and site-specifically integrate into the 28S rDNA loci in their natural host. These characteristics make it possible for R2 retrotransposons to insert large-fragment genes at targeted sites by all-RNA delivery, presenting a new technology for next-generation biotherapeutics. Here, we provide a GFP-intron reporter system to evaluate the activity of the R2 retrotransposons in mammalian cells. Unlike classical all-in-one retrotransposon reporter construct,2,3 this system includes two plasmids, one plasmid for expressing the R2 protein and the other for expressing the R2 donor RNA (Figures 1A and 1B). For the RNA donor plasmid, we designed a GFP-intron cassette, in which the GFP gene is separated by an invertedly-inserted β-globin intron. Inverted intron prevents GFP expression from one promoter, while antisense direction of ORF prevents its expression from the other. Only when the R2 system reverse transcribes the intron-less GFP anti-sense mRNA into DNA and integrates it into the genome, can the GFP protein be expressed (Figure 1C). We placed an SV40-puro-T2A-mCherry cassette on the plasmid expressing RNA donor, so we can use fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) to enrich successfully-transfected cells.
